While this works well, the disadvantage is that it can only infer the status of traffic lights that face the ego vehicle. In contrast, we developed a novel system to infer traffic light statuses from the motion of the ego vehicle and other actors in the scene. This system requires a high performance perception system, which is described in the previous section. Furthermore, it must run offline, since we look at the entire trajectory of a vehicle on the intersection, including its past and future. This trajectory is then matched to the known "lane connectors" in our human-annotated HD map. We can therefore infer that a particular traffic light was set to green or yellow in a particular time window. The advantage is that this approach covers all lanes with observable vehicles. This allows us to realistically simulate the traffic flow in all directions, not just the ego driving direction.']}),Object(h.jsx)("p",{children:Object(h.jsxs)("video",{height:"600",controls:!0,className:o.a.itemInGrid,children:[Object(h.jsx)("source",{src:"/nuplan_traffic_light_demo_211208_dark.mp4",type:"video/mp4"}),"Your browser does not support embedded videos."]})}),Object(h.jsx)("h3",{children:"Scenarios"}),Object(h.jsxs)("p",{children:["To fairly evaluate motion planning models, it is crucial to consider the underlying data distribution.
